facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The epic contains twenty-four thousand verses split into five hundred sargas, concluding Rama's return without any mention of Shani as a footstool.
facts.source_name: Valmiki Ramayana: Critical Edition, Oriental Institute Baroda
facts.text: The Sanskrit Valmiki Ramayana contains no mention of Ravana capturing the nine planets or turning Shani into a staircase or footstool.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The Ramayana narrates the legend of Rama and Sita and her abduction by Ravana... It contains 24,000 verses divided into seven books.
facts.text: The Uttara Kanda of the Valmiki Ramayana chronicles Ravana's conquests over Yama, Kubera, and Indra, yet completely omits the subjugation or imprisonment of the Navagrahas.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: According to traditions associated with the Ananda Ramayana, Ravana once captured the Navagrahas, the nine planetary forces, and placed them beneath the steps of his royal throne.
facts.text: The Sanskrit Ananda Ramayana, composed around the fifteenth century CE, explicitly introduces the narrative of Ravana placing the nine planetary deities beneath the steps of his royal throne.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Written in the traditional Ramayan Panchali form... Ravana laming the leg of Shani dev when he refused to preside over the last horoscope meant for Meghanada's birth.
facts.text: The fifteenth-century Bengali Krittivasi Ramayan incorporates the popular regional legend where Ravana forces the planets into the eleventh house for Meghanada's birth and lames Shani's leg for noncompliance.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: In Goswami Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas it is a sequence of Awadhi chaupais and dohas... but the episode of turning Shani into a staircase is absent.
facts.text: Goswami Tulsidas's sixteenth-century epic Ramcharitmanas contains no verses describing Ravana using Shani Dev as a stepping stone or staircase.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Ravana kept all the planets, including Shani Dev, suppressed beneath his leg or throne facing downwards to nullify the malefic drishti.
facts.text: Widespread North Indian folklore claims that Ravana laid Shani face-down at the foot of his throne so that the deity's malefic gaze could never meet his eyes.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: When Hanuman came to Lanka as Lord Rama's messenger, he heard Shani's cries and freed him from Ravana's imprisonment.
facts.text: Devotional folktales state that Hanuman liberated Shani during the burning of Lanka, giving rise to the custom of worshipping Hanuman to mitigate Saturn's astrological afflictions.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Under a project called the Archaeology of the Ramayana Sites... we found materials such like the northern polished layer and other things which go back to about seven hundred before Christ.
facts.source_name: Archaeological Survey of India (Excavations at Bharadvaja Asrama)
facts.text: The Archaeological Survey of India excavated multiple Ramayana-associated sites under B. B. Lal between 1975 and 1986, documenting early occupational layers dating to approximately 700 BCE but finding no physical traces of epic mythological personages.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Situated on a small hillock, this Brahmanical cave temple is assignable to the 6th century CE, containing beautifully carved sculptures including Shiva and Ardhanarishvara.
facts.text: The Archaeological Survey of India dates the rock-cut Ravan Phadi cave shrine at Aihole to the sixth century CE, dedicated to classical Shaivite relief sculptures rather than epic battles.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The presence of Navagraha lintel suggests, states Mevissen, that the temple complex must be dated after 600 CE.
facts.source_name: Archaeological Survey of India / Bateshwar Documentation
facts.text: Archaeological excavations of temple doorways from around 600 CE, such as those conserved by the ASI at the Bateshwar complex in Madhya Pradesh, consistently depict the Navagrahas as an honoured celestial panel rather than subjugated figures under a throne.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Known in temple sculpture as Ravananugraha, this scene turns up from Elephanta to Ellora... depicting Ravana attempting to uproot Kailash and trapped beneath it.
facts.source_name: Archaeological Survey of India / Ellora Caves Documentation
facts.text: The eighth-century CE rock-cut Kailash Temple at Ellora showcases the prominent Ravananugraha relief depicting Ravana being subdued under Mount Kailash by Shiva's toe rather than conquering planetary forces.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Scholars generally agree that the first and seventh books of the Ramayana were later additions, though traditional commentators regard all seven kandas as authentic.
facts.text: Textual scholars and Indologists dispute the date and composition of the Ramayana, with critical philologists arguing that the Uttara Kanda is a post-Valmiki interpolation whereas traditional commentators assert that all seven kandas form an integral, unified epic.
